name: Grenada
prevalence_note: ECCB, CSIRT Grenada & Royal Grenada Police Force (RGPF) 2025-2026: bank/social-media phishing and OTP capture, fake lottery prize advance-fee calls, customs/parcel fee impersonation, and unlicensed crypto pyramid & AI voice-cloning scams dominate.
cross_border_note: Uses +1-473 within NANP and the Eastern Caribbean Currency Union (XCD); regional +1 spoofing and WhatsApp account takeovers are widespread.

scams.name: Bank Card / OTP Vishing & Social-Media Account Phishing
scams.name_en: ECCB & CSIRT Grenada-warned phishing call or message stealing banking OTPs and credentials
scams.signals_en: Caller or message poses as an ECCU commercial bank or platform support warning of suspicious activity and asking for one-time codes, full card details, or clicking a verification link.
scams.legit_en: ECCB and Grenada CSIRT warn citizens never to disclose banking passwords, card details, or one-time codes to unsolicited callers or links.
bait_tactics: Say you are heading into St. George's town shortly and will check directly at the bank counter.
Pretend the verification SMS has not come through due to weak signal in your parish.
Ask the caller to verify which Eastern Caribbean bank branch issued your card.

scams.name: Fake Lottery Prize & Customs Parcel Clearance Fee Scam
scams.name_en: Caller claiming a lottery win or detained overseas barrel/parcel requiring an upfront fee
scams.signals_en: Unsolicited call or WhatsApp message stating the victim won a cash sweepstakes or has a gift parcel held at customs, demanding an advance payment before release.
scams.legit_en: ECCB highlights fake prize scams requiring upfront payment as a classic fraud indicator, and real Grenada customs duties are paid at official ports.
bait_tactics: Ask why the clearance fee cannot be deducted from the cash winnings before delivery.
Say you will check at the St. George's port customs office yourself.
Pretend you need time to find your reading glasses to copy down the shipping company details.

scams.name: Unlicensed Crypto Pyramid & AI Voice-Cloned Relative Scam
scams.name_en: ECCB-warned zero-risk crypto recruitment scheme or AI-cloned family emergency request
scams.signals_en: Promotes high-yield, zero-risk investment/recruitment clubs converting EC dollars into crypto, or uses AI-replicated voice/WhatsApp messages of a relative asking for emergency money.
scams.legit_en: ECCB and ECSRC require securities/investment operators to hold valid licences, and family requests should be verified on a known phone line.
bait_tactics: Ask for the company's Eastern Caribbean Securities Regulatory Commission (ECSRC) licence status.
If the caller sounds like a relative in distress, ask a private family question or call their usual line directly.
Say your funds are tied up in a fixed deposit that cannot be withdrawn this month.
